title: Fasting: Training in Sabr and Taqwa
summary: At the age of 7-9, a child can try partial fasting as training, since fasting is not obligatory for him before puberty. When his practice ends, serve him his food and complete your own fast until sunset; stop the practice if he becomes dizzy, very tired, or very thirsty, and consult the doctor if he is ill or takes medication. We focus on understanding the meaning of fasting (sabr, mindfulness of Allah, feeling for the poor) rather than merely abstaining from food.
try_this: Today: Sit with your child and agree on a partial-fasting plan for the coming Ramadan, if he wants to and is in good health: he fasts part of the day suited to his ability, such as until Dhuhr, and may stop whenever he gets tired. Then ask him: What helps you be patient when you are hungry?
reflection_prompts: How does your child behave when he feels hunger?
What question did he ask about fasting?
